description: Six stand-alone journeys use food to enter very different cultures: Shanghai's markets, Japanese culinary discipline, a Cornish Christmas, Italian opera, the Mississippi Delta blues and Germany's regional traditions.

s07e01.description: Rick explores Shanghai's culinary roots through wet markets, dumpling houses and home cooking, tracing dishes such as red-braised pork and hairy crab through a city where old regional traditions survive relentless modernisation.

s07e02.description: Rick travels through Japan to understand the restraint, seasonality and technique behind its cuisine, then returns home to cook a banquet for the Japanese ambassador using what he has learned.

s07e03.description: A Cornish Christmas mixes wassailing, the Eden Project ice rink and the voices of the Fisherman's Friends with local beer, cider and a generous festive banquet built from Cornish ingredients.

s07e04.description: Food and music share the stage as Rick follows Verdi, Rossini and Puccini through Italy, showing how the composers, their regions and the dishes around them belong to the same cultural landscape.

s07e05.description: Based at the Shack Up Inn, Rick travels the Mississippi Delta through blues music and the foods embedded in its songs, including fried chicken, greens, catfish and black-eyed peas.

s07e06.description: Rick travels through Germany in search of the regional cooking obscured by clichés, finding local sausages, bread, beer, preserved foods and other culinary traditions that vary sharply from one part of the country to another.
